messages:
alex.s (support): ACME prod reporting severe p99 spikes since 14:18 UTC. p95 ~300ms, p99 6-10s. Customer says requests hang in queue before worker accept. No 5xx, no auth errors. sample req IDs: req-abc123, req-def456. 

alex.s (support): Repro steps from customer: sustained streaming workload ~120rps, many long generations. They included a short log: 
```
[14:19:02] req=req-abc123 accept_delay=5200ms service_latency=40ms
[14:19:07] req=req-def456 accept_delay=6100ms service_latency=38ms
```

jamie (eng-oncall): thx @alex.s. Can you paste tenant id and admission metrics? Any 429s or circuit drops? Also need route/model they hit.

alex.s (support): Tenant=acme-42. No 429s in customer logs. Admission queue length snapshot from our metrics: 14:10 -> 30; 14:18 -> 620; 14:22 -> 480. Route=hosted/gpt-large-v2 (streaming).

maya (eng-sre): I'm looking at the us-west-2 serving pool for acme-42: node-9 GPU %util ~98, worker threads saturated. Autoscaler didn't add new workers because reserved_capacity cap hit (reserved_count=10 for this tenant). Batching backlog climbed; continuous-batching max_inflight is currently set to 256 per pool which allowed big batches but exceeded worker scheduling window -> queue growth.

jamie (eng-oncall): hypothesis: tenant burst bypassed warm pool and hit the reserved grid, saturating it. Two immediate mitigations: (A) enable tenant warm_start so requests can warm workers (B) add a routing fallback to a lower-latency variant (gpt-medium-ql) to shed load while preserving correctness (C) temporarily raise admission limit for acme-42 if capacity exists. Which is lowest-risk?

alex.s (support): Customer is mid-launch, wants ASAP. Prefer (B) then (A). They asked we avoid raising concurrency unless we can confirm spare capacity.

maya (eng-sre): I can flip (A)+(B). Patching routing fallback first (safe, quick), then hot_start. Patch command below.

maya (eng-sre): ```bash
# enable hot_start and fallback model for tenant
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.internal/v1/admin/tenants/acme-42/config" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"hot_start": true, "fallback_model": "gpt-medium-ql"}'
```

deploy-bot: rolling out acme-42-config-6951200001 -> 3 hosts (canary 1/3).

deploy-bot: rollout success acme-42-config-6951200001 on 3/3 hosts, version=v2-hotstart-2026-03-17.

alex.s (support): Customer reports visible improvement ~45s after patch. p99 dropped to ~1.2s, p95 steady. They say most requests are routed to fallback variant while warm-start kicks in. :thumbsup: 

ravi (customer-success): I'll send an update to ACME: explain fallback + hot-start, recommend capacity commit for Dedicated if they expect sustained bursts.

jamie (eng-oncall): follow-up action items: - open postmortem to review autoscaler thresholds and reserved capacity behavior - consider tenant-level burst allowance that temporarily extends reserved_count for short windows - add alert: admission_queue_length > 200 for 2+ minutes -> page eng-sre - evaluate lowering continuous-batching max_inflight to reduce scheduling tail latency

alex.s (support): Opening ENG-7234 and assigning to eng-sre (maya). I'll include uploaded metrics, logs, and customer repro.

maya (eng-sre): saved metrics+logs to /logs/incidents/6951200001 (retain 30d). Short repro note for eng team: run the loadgen below against hosted/gpt-large-v2 without warm_start to reproduce queueing tail.

maya (eng-sre): ```bash
# repro: sustained 120 rps streaming generations
./loadgen --host https://api.redwood.prod --tenant acme-42 --rps 120 \n  --streaming --seq-len 1024 --duration 300s --auth "Bearer CUSTOMER_TOKEN"
```

alex.s (support): Customer confirmed workaround acceptable for now. They'll consider Dedicated commit. Closing urgent escalation but keeping ENG-7234 open for follow-up. :eyes:
